tasks.short: Assign designers and explain the required creative work

steps.what: Assign staff after discussing design ideas, skills, workload and required drawings

tasks.design: Keep assignment discussions with the designer. Use {PROJECT} to view and record commitments during that discussion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Creative suitability and actual capacity need discussion with the people doing the work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing project records can support the conversation without a new allocation engine.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing who can resolve an unfamiliar design problem and negotiating conflicting deadlines.
tasks.human_edge: The designer connects creative intent to individual strengths and checks agreement.
tasks.altitude: Assign coherent creative responsibilities rather than distribute isolated drawing tickets.

reach.learn: Which assignments need mentoring or different deadlines

evidence.claim: Staff assignment in this task depends on creative judgement and negotiation; a saving is not established.

assumptions: Boundary is staff assignment and briefing, not production of their drawings.
The designer asks staff about current commitments during s1; no free structured capacity or competence flags are assumed.
Use the existing project view first.
No incremental upkeep is claimed because no new automation or data feed is introduced.
unknowns: How assignments and commitments are currently recorded
research_questions: Do assignment problems arise from missing workload visibility or unresolved creative scope?

already_counted.description: Capacity discussion and recording agreed assignments

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net saving are zero. Assignment discussion is retained in full.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan around site space, traffic and safety constraints

steps.what: Inspect location-specific conditions and plan space, traffic flow and safety arrangements

tasks.design: Keep site inspection and planning with the designer and venue specialists. Annotate the existing drawings in {DOCS} as part of that work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Drawings alone do not establish actual circulation conditions or safety requirements.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing digital drawings can carry site annotations without a new planning system.
tasks.still_hard: Reconciling crowd movement, physical restrictions and venue-specific safety advice.
tasks.human_edge: The designer observes the location and resolves conflicting requirements with accountable specialists.
tasks.altitude: Integrate physical constraints into a usable site plan.

reach.task: Explain site restrictions and operating conditions
reach.learn: Which layout choices need specialist review

evidence.claim: Site planning needs observation and contextual safety judgement; image generation does not establish those conditions.

assumptions: Boundary includes inspection and planning, not construction or formal safety certification.
The designer observes and records dimensions and flow constraints in s1; venue specialists supply restrictions during the same discussion. No ready safety or clearance flags are assumed.
Use existing drawings and annotation tools first.
No incremental upkeep is added because no automated site model is proposed.
unknowns: Who can approve venue safety arrangements
research_questions: Which planning decisions require fresh site observations rather than existing drawings?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero gross and net saving. No separate administrative baseline is established.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Arrange suitable specimens and graphics for exhibits

steps.what: Obtain specimens or graphics offers with provenance, rights, condition, cost and delivery details
Draft a comparison of offers against required exhibit use and acquisition conditions

loop.purpose: Compare suitability and restrictions expressed in different supplier descriptions
loop.input: Offers and exhibit requirements from s1
loop.output: Comparison with source passages and unresolved conditions
loop.check: Designer checks every cost, right, condition and suitability statement against its offer
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unresolved terms return to direct supplier discussion
loop.why_not_simpler: Offer descriptions and use restrictions need contextual interpretation rather than a common price formula

steps.what: Select specimens or graphics and agree acquisition and delivery with the supplier

tasks.design: Use {DOCS} to compare actual supplier offers, then let the designer resolve rights and suitability. The designer places the acquisition through {EMAIL} after checking the exact terms.
tasks.previous_blocker: Offers combine narrative descriptions, restrictions and practical delivery conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: A document assistant can draft a source-linked comparison for review.
tasks.still_hard: Establishing authenticity, condition and rights and obtaining workable delivery commitments.
tasks.human_edge: The designer judges exhibit suitability and negotiates the acquisition.
tasks.altitude: Evaluate acquisition conditions together with the exhibit purpose.

reach.task: Clarify rights, condition and delivery commitments

evidence.claim: An assistant could draft a comparison of narrative offers; the suitability judgement and time saving remain unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is arranging acquisition; physical conservation and installation are separate work.

Suppliers produce dated descriptions, provenance, rights, prices and delivery terms in their replies; s1 includes requesting, collecting and checking them. Missing facts remain questions, never inferred permissions.
Use existing document assistance before building a procurement integration.
Supplier clarifications in s3 arise after comparison; normal supplier response effort is unchanged, not a claimed saving.
research_questions: Does a reviewed comparison shorten offer assessment without increasing missed restrictions?

incremental.description: Maintain the comparison instructions and sample source accuracy
Check document access and assistant configuration

approvals.approved_version: Exact supplier, item, quantity, price, rights, condition and delivery terms; changes require renewed review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+21+35=91; gross 9 minus focal upkeep 3 gives net 6 as an E1 design scenario. Reported range 0-2 allows for sparse offers and extra rights clarification.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design and produce decorative displays and materials

steps.what: Establish display requirements and draft decorative concepts for the actual event location

loop.purpose: Explore decorative visual concepts from a designer-authored brief
loop.input: Designer records event purpose, site dimensions, colours, materials and restrictions within s1
loop.check: Designer checks fit with the brief and rejects invented dimensions or material properties
loop.stop: Two alternatives and one revision, then continue with manual design
loop.why_not_simpler: Visual composition requires creative interpretation rather than a fixed layout template

steps.what: Develop constructible designs and produce displays and decorative materials

tasks.design: Use {OTHER}, a visual design editor, for reviewed concept alternatives. The designer develops workable details and physically produces the decoration.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exploring alternative visual compositions can take repeated sketching.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest describes image generation and editing capability in Adobe Creative Studio [S1].
tasks.still_hard: Material behaviour, constructibility and producing pieces that work at the actual location.
tasks.human_edge: The designer turns an illustrative idea into a coherent physical display.
tasks.altitude: Connect visual exploration to practical production.

reach.task: Confirm event needs and site restrictions

evidence.claim: Adobe Creative Studio supports image generation and editing; that capability does not establish constructible display designs.
The concept-stage saving is an unmeasured scenario and excludes physical production.

assumptions: Boundary includes this task's decorative design and production, not set concepts counted under another task.
Designer captures dimensions, materials and restrictions in s1 and checks them during s2; the generator never produces authoritative geometry or safety flags.
Use the visual editor already available before introducing another service.
Most time remains in detailed design and physical production.
unknowns: Share of time spent on concept sketching
Image-editor access and permitted material use
research_questions: Do reviewed concept alternatives reduce sketching time without more production rework?

incremental.description: Maintain visual instructions and review recurring concept errors

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=14+80=94; gross 6 minus focal upkeep 2 gives net 4 in an E1 scenario. Range 0-2 allows for already quick sketches and extra revision.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Coordinate creative work and acquisition while producing practical site-specific designs.
reach: Ask venue specialists about actual constraints
Resolve specimen rights directly with suppliers
skills_to_grow: Separate illustrative concepts from production specifications
role.ambitious_version: A designer who tests visual directions quickly and keeps responsibility for staffing, acquisition and physical feasibility.
